trust_decision.summary: Whether an XML request body may resolve external DTDs, external general/parameter entities and XIncludes is decided once, by the shared SAXParserFactory built in the org.http4s.scalaxml package object; both entity decoders obtain their parser from that single factory.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says only 'XML External Entity (XXE) processing issue', so the first thing an engineer greps for is XML parsing: XML.loadXML(source, saxParser) inside the implicit xmlDecoder that Request.as[Elem] reaches. The protection actually lives one file away in the package-object default, not at this call site.

fix_sites.entry_point: org.http4s.scalaxml.xmlDecoder[F] (implicit EntityDecoder) and org.http4s.scalaxml.xml[F] (deprecated EntityDecoder), both via saxFactory.newSAXParser()
fix_sites.module_kind: library codec module (http4s-scala-xml) - package-object default configuration

fix_sites.entry_point: public trait ElemInstances: visibility widened from `protected` to `protected[scalaxml]` so the test suite can inspect saxFactory; no security behaviour of its own
fix_sites.module_kind: library codec module - public trait member

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The deprecated, blocking `xml[F]` decoder is annotated @deprecated("Blocks. Use xmlDecoder with an Async constraint.", "0.23.12"), is not implicit, and is never exercised by the pinned test suite, so a solver can argue it is a superseded legacy path that the advisory did not cover and that need not be hardened.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Documents that legitimately carry an internal DTD subset with their own entity declarations (e.g. `<!DOCTYPE greeting [<!ENTITY who "world">]>`) parse today and would be rejected outright by `disallow-doctype-decl=true`; the decoder converts the resulting SAXParseException into a 400 MalformedMessageBodyFailure. A narrower fix (disable only external entities/DTD loading) keeps internal-DTD documents working.

O6_input_shapes: XML body with a DOCTYPE carrying an external SYSTEM/PUBLIC identifier
external general entity declared in a DOCTYPE and referenced in element content
external parameter entity (% name SYSTEM "...";) and parameter-entity expansion
XInclude directive in the document body
DTD URI resolution for a referenced DTD

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a NodeSeq/Document entity decoder written with XML.loadString or XML.withSAXParser instead of saxFactory.newSAXParser()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The trait already ships two decoders over the same sink for the same type, and scala-xml users routinely ask for NodeSeq codecs; a contributor would reach for the convenience loader rather than a factory.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second package object / `all` object, or a public ElemInstances subclass, overriding saxFactory with its own unhardened factory
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: saxFactory is an abstract member of the public ElemInstances trait (ElemInstances.scala:38), so instantiating the trait twice is a supported extension point.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an xmlValidatingDecoder that deliberately allows DTD/DOCTYPE processing for documents that need it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Validating XML is a real consumer need, and the natural place to relax the disallow-doctype default is next to the existing decoders.

O9_family: CWE-611 improper restriction of XML external entity references (XXE) in the SAX parser configuration shared by the scala-xml entity decoders

O10_build.toolchain: sbt 1.12.13 with sbt-http4s-org 2.0.6 plugin; JVM temurin 8/11/17
O10_build.project_tests: ScalaXmlSuite (munit + munit-cats-effect + scalacheck-xml): about 21 encode/decode, charset and parse-error tests, run with `sbt scalaXml/test`; at the pinned commit there are no XXE, DOCTYPE or entity tests at all.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Set external-general-entities=false on the shared factory and stop there (the textbook one-liner), leaving external parameter entities, external DTD loading, DOCTYPE handling and XInclude open.
